v: #### Self-reproducible output (JASP / jamovi / SPSS Viewer / Jupyter notebook)

2 JASP/jamovi/SPSS-Viewer/notebook files bundle the analyses and their saved results together, so the reported statistics are recoverable from the files itself, with nothing re-run. We extracted 5 result tables (46 individual statistics), typed with the STATO ontology, and export them as a statistical-output JSON document (in the logs) and as queryable rows.
1 statistical test reported in the manuscript text was checked against the extracted analysis output: 1 matched (1 fully, 0 partially) — 100% found.

Some reported values were only found alongside OTHER components after being separated from their own originally-reported neighbours (e.g. a mean split from its own confidence interval). The "Plausible" column marks whether that split is well-supported: TRUE when the pieces still trace back to the same underlying variable (via the output's own row labels), FALSE when no such link was found — a FALSE match is not necessarily wrong, but is worth checking against its own Source file/Analysis columns before treating it as confirmed.

```{r}
#| echo: false


# table data --------------------------------------
table <- structure(list(Reported = "t=3.75 df=67 p=<0.001", Found = TRUE, 
    Confidence = "full", Plausible = "yes", "Matched values" = "t=3.75, df=67, p=<0.001", 
    "Not matched" = "", "Source file" = "sample.omv", Analysis = "ttestOneS"), row.names = c(NA, 
-1L), class = "data.frame")

# display table -----------------------------------
metacheck::report_table(table, "auto", 15, FALSE)
```

-  We assessed 2 self-reproducible output files (JASP/jamovi/SPSS-Viewer/Mplus) instead of R code.
-  46 statistics stored from the extracted output.
-  1 of 1 reported test matched (100%).
-  We found no R code files to assess for reproducibility.
